You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"East Pennant irrigation","question":"Can lands staff certify the pump telemetry report?","claims":{"A":"Pump P9 reached at least 40 litres per minute on its first test.","B":"P9 had a 3-inch intake installed on the test bench.","C":"Technicians powered P9 on Wednesday."},"sources":{"S1":"the bench register specifies a 2-inch intake installed.","S2":"maintenance engineer circulated a design curve showing 43 litres per minute with a similar intake and wrote that 40 seemed safe.","S3":"bench activation register confirms P9 powered on Wednesday."},"follow_up":{"S4":"an independent calibrated meter records P9 at 43 litres per minute during its first test."}}

Claim B is contradicted by S1, which specifies a 2-inch intake installed, not 3-inch. Claim C is supported by S3, the bench activation register confirming P9 was powered on Wednesday. S2 provides provisional support for A but is less direct than S4."}

parsed.note: Claim A is supported decisively by S4, an independent calibrated meter recording 43 litres per minute during P9's first test, confirming it reached at least 40 litres per minute. Claim B is contradicted by S1, which specifies a 2-inch intake installed, not 3-inch. Claim C is supported by S3, the bench activation register confirming P9 was powered on Wednesday. S2 provides provisional support for A but is less direct than S4.
